sources.entry: Qilin Editor - Text editor for exact sciences with built-in KaTeX/AsciiMath support.

summary.one_liner: Qilin is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed desktop text editor for exact sciences with built-in KaTeX and AsciiMath support.
summary.what_it_does: Qilin is a text editor aimed at mathematical and scientific writing, with support for KaTeX and AsciiMath notation. It is built on Chromium and Node.js and is described as working on each desktop platform. It can be extended through several plugins and themes. Documents can be exported as HTML, PDF, or Markdown. The README also lists developer commands for preparing, building, starting, watching, and cleaning the project, plus lint-fix scripts. Installation details are in an INSTALL.md file and usage questions are directed to the project Wiki.
use_cases: writing scientific documents with math formulas
exporting documents to Markdown or HTML
extending a desktop editor with plugins and themes
hacking on an Electron-style Chromium and Node.js editor
notable: Built-in KaTeX and AsciiMath math support for exact sciences
Exports documents to HTML, PDF, and Markdown
Extensible through plugins and themes, plus a Qilin package manager (preapre-qpm command)
Fully hackable codebase under the MIT license with an additional patent grant
caveats: README says the project is still in development and may not suit daily intensive use
The sole active maintainer states they cannot provide regular updates and welcomes help
